content: For individuals over 12 years of age, administer 15 to 30 milliliters of the medication orally every 15 minutes until vomiting ceases. Do not exceed five doses within one hour. For children aged 2 to 12 years, administer 5 to 10 milliliters orally every 15 minutes until vomiting stops, ensuring no more than five doses are given in one hour. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established for children under 2 years of age. Patients should avoid consuming fluids for at least 15 minutes after taking the medication. If symptoms persist, worsen, or recur, consult a healthcare provider promptly. Individuals with diabetes should seek medical advice before self-medicating with this product. Do not exceed five doses within one hour; if this occurs, contact a healthcare provider immediately. This medication is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients, as well as those with hereditary fructose intolerance. Common side effects may include abdominal pain and diarrhea. In the event of an overdose, if the individual experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for every individual. Always consult a healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. For medical advice about side effects, U.S. residents should contact their doctor, while Canadian residents should do the same. This information was last revised in May 2024.
